newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end up on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end up on speculation.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Friday on speculative buying from retail investors but trading was slow, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 3,416 yuan ($411) per tonne, rising six yuan. It opened at 3,411 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,418 and a low of 3,401 yuan.
May rose one to 3,351, September fell five to 3,425, November put on 25 to 3,440 and January 1998 contract was unchanged at 3,430 yuan.
Combined volume fell to 21,500 tonnes from 26,000.
Traders said many investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of the weekend with only some retail investors pushing prices up.
"Many investors were in a weekend mood and speculators dominated the day's trading," one trader said.
"Market sentiment improved a lot after the rises over the past few days," he added.
Traders said soybeans were likely to maintain their upward trend in the short term.
